headline: A document with apparatus, not an app with content
overview: The page a reader actually came for. The lead answers first; contents, inline citations and the other-language versions sit around it without competing for attention.

steps.title: Lead section first, apparatus around it
steps.description: The lead answers the question before any navigation appears. Contents, references and language links are all present but subordinate — the page is a document with apparatus, not an app with content in it.
steps.screenshotAlt: The lead section of the Pointillism article

steps.title: Sections carry their own citations
steps.action: Scrolled to the first substantive section.
steps.description: Every claim is footnoted at the point it's made rather than in a bibliography at the end. On a long article that's the difference between a reader being able to check one sentence and having to trust the whole page.
steps.screenshotAlt: A body section of the article with inline citations

steps.title: The same article, in every language that has one
steps.description: Each language is a separate article with its own editors and its own revision history, not a translation of the English one. They're linked as siblings rather than derived from a source — which is why the list is a navigation surface and not a locale toggle.
steps.screenshotAlt: The language selector listing other-language versions

annotations.text: Captured as a step inside this feature, not as a separate `article-fr` feature. A locale is an axis through a feature; cataloguing it separately would inflate the feature count without documenting anything new.

tips: Each language version is an independent article with its own history — the language list is navigation between siblings, not a translation switch.
